messages.subject: checkAlleles alternative for 4way design
parts:
Hi All,

I am working with a 4way mapping population of 400 individuals genotyped at ~1200 SNP loci. I used Stacks to call genotypes, estimated my original map using JoinMap, and have now loaded all my geno and phenotype data into R/qtl. I am performing the initial data diagnostics such as checking for segregation distortion and counting crossovers etc. but have found that 'checkAlleles' does not work for a 4way design. I can use 'calc.errorlod' to get a list of genotypes that are potentially wrong but I am having trouble coming up with a threshold for which markers to keep or discard, and when to throw out the whole marker vs. the specific datapoint. When I re-estimated my map in rqtl several chromosomes were inflated to 6000cM. I believe this strongly suggests I have some mis-called genotypes or markers out of order.

Is there a rigorous way to come up with a threshold or should I get rid of everything with a LOD >4.0?
Are there any other functions that do not work for a 4way design?

Thanks,
Liz

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] checkAlleles alternative for 4way design
parts:
checkAlleles serves a somewhat different purpose from calc.errorlod. checkAlleles is looking for cases where the parental alleles should be switched (a marker's genotypes are strongly associated with genotypes at other markers, but with recombination fractions near 1 rather than near 0). The error LOD scores are looking for tight double-crossovers indicative of genotyping errors. The error LOD scores might show the former, but probably the genetic map will be distorted which could make the error LOD scores less informative.

You could do a plot of the LOD scores vs rec. fracs. from est.rf, and look for cases where LOD is large and rf is >> 0.5.

data(fake.4way)
fake.4way <- est.rf(fake.4way)
rf <- pull.rf(fake.4way)
lod <- pull.rf(fake.4way, "lod")
plot(as.numeric(rf), as.numeric(lod))

I think there are a number of other functions that don't work for the 4-way design, but unfortunately I don't have a list of which ones they are.

karl
